questions.question: Explain two Muslim beliefs about angels.

points.text: 1) Jibril is the chief angel who brought revelation from Allah to the prophets, most importantly delivering the Qur'an to Muhammad over 23 years. Without Jibril, Muslims would not have the Qur'an. 2) Raqib and Atid are recording angels who write down every good and bad deed a person does. questions.question: "Belief in angels is not important for Muslims today." Evaluate this statement.

points.text: Some might argue angels are irrelevant because they are invisible and cannot be proven scientifically. However, for Muslims, belief in angels is essential — it is one of the Six Articles of Faith. Angels demonstrate that Allah is actively involved in the world, they record human deeds for Judgement Day, and Jibril delivered the Qur'an itself.
